1	# Mid-century modern house (Eichler / Palm Springs): FORM PLAN (architect)
2	
3	Identity: a long, low post-and-beam house in white stucco and dark timber, with a pale near-flat gable roof, deep eaves and beam ends that stick out past them. The street face is blank apart from a tan ledgestone feature wall, a clerestory strip and an orange front door. A flat carport stands to the west with a teal and white car in front of it. The back is all glass, with a kidney pool behind it.
4	Grid: x 0..33 (west→east, along the street), z 0..33 (z=0 sidewalk on the NORTH street side, z=33 back lot line), y = height.
5	Ground top = y=0 (bedding y=-1). House floor slab y=1. Walls y=1..5. Roof y=6..7. Chimney to y=8.
6	Structural rhythm: **beam lines every 3 cells at x = 10,13,16,19,22,25,28,31.** Every post, beam and beam end sits on one of these lines.
7	
8	## SITE
9	
10	| mass / feature | x0..x1 | y0..y1 | z0..z1 | notes |
11	|---|---|---|---|---|
12	| Lot ground (bedding) | 0..33 | -1 | 0..33 | dirt, under everything except the pool |
13	| Sidewalk | 0..33 | 0 | 0 | smooth_stone, one row along the street |
14	| Driveway (concrete) | 1..8 | 0 | 1..21 | smooth_stone; joint rows of light_gray_concrete at z=4,8,12,16 |
15	| Front yard (desert) | 9..33 | 0 | 1..7 | sand; gravel beds at x=22..30 z=1..5 and x=10..16 z=1..5 |
16	| Stepping-pad path | 18..20 | 0 | 1, 3, 5 | three 3x1 smooth_stone pads in the sand (sand between them) |
17	| Entry landing | 18..20 | 0 | 6..7 | smooth_stone, under the eave |
18	| Side strips | 0 (x) / 32..33 | 0 | 1..25 | x=0: sand; x=32..33: sand |
19	| MAIN HOUSE (shell) | 10..31 | 1..5 | 8..25 | 22 wide x 18 deep; walls on the perimeter |
20	| Main roof (incl. overhangs) | 9..32 | 6..7 | 6..27 | low gable, ridge along x; see ROOFS |
21	| Beam ends (exposed tails) | each beam line | 5 | 5 and 28 | 1 cell past the roof edge, front and back |
22	| ATRIUM (open courtyard, open to the sky) | 17..21 | 1..open | 12..17 | 5x6; glass ring on x=16, x=22, z=11, z=18 |
23	| Entry recess | 18..20 | 2..4 | 8 | air niche; the door wall sits back at z=9 |
24	| Stone feature wall | 11..17 | 1..4 | 7 | freestanding 1-thick leaf, 1 proud of the north wall (z=8) |
25	| CARPORT | 0..9 | 1..5 | 7..21 | flat roof deck y=5 on posts; open N, W; screen at S |
26	| Carport posts | x=1 | 1..4 | z=8, 14, 20 | dark_oak_log, 1x1 |
27	| Carport beams | 0..9 | 4 | z=8, 14, 20 | dark_oak_log axis x; the deck sits on them |
28	| Carport breeze-block screen | 1..9 | 1..4 | 21 | pierced: checkerboard of white_concrete and AIR (holes left open) |
29	| CAR (reserved, see RESERVED) | 3..5 | 1..2 | 1..7 | parked nose to the street on the driveway, in front of the carport |
30	| Chimney (fireplace part) | 20..21 | 2..8 | 21..22 | rises through the roof 1 above the ridge band |
31	| Back patio | 10..31 | 0 | 26..28 | smooth_stone, under/behind the south eave |
32	| Pool deck | 11..24 | 0 | 29..33 | smooth_stone around the pool |
33	| KIDNEY POOL (reserved) | 13..22 | -2..0 | 29..32 | see RESERVED for the exact cells |
34	| Back lawn | 0..10 & 25..33 | 0 | 26..33 | grass_block (x=0..9 z=22..33 included) |
35	| Palms | (12,3), (30,4), (29,31) | 1..7 | — | jungle trunk + crown, reserved |
36	| Cactus cluster | 23..29 | 1..3 | 2..4 | on the gravel bed, reserved |
37	| Mailbox | 9 | 1..2 | 1 | low post + box at the head of the driveway |
38	
39	## ROOFS
40	
41	**Main roof: built BY HAND (no preset).** No `$MCD roof` preset fits a mid-century roof: every preset has a pitch of 0.5 or more, and the brief wants a very low gable. The low pitch is the identity, so the roof is a stepped slab gable with the ridge running E-W (along x), its slopes facing the street and the garden. It covers x=9..32 (1 cell of overhang at each gable end) and z=6..27 (2 cells of overhang front and back):
42	
43	| band | z rows | block / half | y |
44	|---|---|---|---|
45	| A, eaves | 6..10 and 23..27 | bottom slab | 6 |
46	| B | 11..13 and 20..22 | top slab | 6 |
47	| C | 14..15 and 18..19 | bottom slab | 7 |
48	| Ridge | 16..17 | top slab | 7 |
49	
50	- Rise: 1.5 blocks over a 10-cell half-span, the near-flat Eichler gable. The highest point is y=7.
51	- **Fascia:** the outermost ring (z=6, z=27, x=9, x=32) uses dark_oak_slab at the same half as its band, so a dark line runs round the eave.
52	- **Atrium hole:** no roof over x=17..21, z=12..17. The edge of the hole is dark_oak_slab, as fascia.
53	- **Chimney hole:** no roof at x=20..21, z=21..22.
54	- **Under band C:** the y=6 cells over the interior are air (a raised ceiling vault). The two gable ends close them with glass (see OPENINGS), and so does the atrium ring where it crosses band C (x=16 and x=22, y=6, z=14..17, glass).
55	- **Beams (exposed):** dark_oak_log with axis z, at y=5 on each beam line x=10,13,...,31, running z=5..28. They pass through the north and south header courses. Inside the house they are ceiling beams with 3 cells of headroom (y=2..4) below them; between the beams the ceiling is at y=5. Outside, they carry the overhang and stick out 1 cell past the fascia at z=5 and z=28. Where the beam on x=19 crosses the atrium it stays as an open beam over the courtyard.
56	- **Carport roof:** a flat deck, hand built: smooth_stone_slab (bottom half) at y=5 over x=0..9, z=7..21, with a dark_oak_slab fascia on its outer edges (x=0, z=7, z=21). It sits one level below the main roof's west eave (x=9, y=6). The two horizontal planes layered against each other are the mid-century signature.
57	
58	## FACADES
59	
60	All walls are white stucco (white_concrete). Every outer wall has the same three layers:
61	
62	| layer | y | block |
63	|---|---|---|
64	| Base (slab edge) | 1 | smooth_stone |
65	| Body | 2..4 | white stucco, glass or posts |
66	| Header course | 5 | dark_oak_planks, a continuous dark band under the eave |
67	
68	The beam ends cross the header.
69	
70	**North (street, z=8): mostly blank.** From west to east:
71	- **x=10..17:** blank stucco. In front of it, the **ledgestone feature wall** stands at z=7, x=11..17, y=1..4. It is 1 proud and freestanding, mud_bricks mixed with ~25% packed_mud for the stacked-stone texture. Its top is capped with mud_brick_slab at y=5, but only between the beam lines (x=11,12,14,15,17); the beams at x=13 and x=16 pass over it.
72	- **x=18..20:** the **entry recess**, 1 deep: the door wall sits at z=9. On it, x=19 is the door, with an orange_concrete transom at y=4. x=18 and x=20 are orange_concrete panels at y=2..4, which makes a bold 3-wide orange door set in white. Reveals at x=17 (stone) and x=21 (stucco).
73	- **x=21..31:** stucco with the **clerestory strip** in the top course of the body (y=4): glass at x=22..24, 26..27 and 29..30, and dark_oak_log mullions on the beam lines x=25 and x=28. Below it the wall is blank (bedroom wing).
74	- The 2-cell eave (z=6..7) shades the whole face; the beam ends at z=5 give the rhythm.
75	
76	**South (garden, z=25): a wall of glass.** The only stucco is the base (y=1) and the header (y=5). Thin dark posts (dark_oak_log, vertical) stand at y=2..4 on every beam line. Between the posts are full-height glass_pane walls (y=2..4), with sliding-door gaps (see OPENINGS). The eave overhangs to z=27 and the beam ends to z=28.
77	
78	**West (x=10, facing the carport) and East (x=31):** stucco with base and header. Above the header, the gable end shows a glass clerestory band at y=6, z=14..19, between header and roof, and the fascia steps over it. Dark posts at the corners (x=10/31, z=8 and z=25) run y=2..4 on all four corners.
79

# Mid-century modern house (Eichler / Palm Springs): FORM PLAN (architect)

Identity: a long, low post-and-beam house in white stucco and dark timber, with a pale near-flat gable roof, deep eaves and beam ends that stick out past them. The street face is blank apart from a tan ledgestone feature wall, a clerestory strip and an orange front door. A flat carport stands to the west with a teal and white car in front of it. The back is all glass, with a kidney pool behind it.
Grid: x 0..33 (west→east, along the street), z 0..33 (z=0 sidewalk on the NORTH street side, z=33 back lot line), y = height.
Ground top = y=0 (bedding y=-1). House floor slab y=1. Walls y=1..5. Roof y=6..7. Chimney to y=8.
Structural rhythm: **beam lines every 3 cells at x = 10,13,16,19,22,25,28,31.** Every post, beam and beam end sits on one of these lines.

## SITE

| mass / feature | x0..x1 | y0..y1 | z0..z1 | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lot ground (bedding) | 0..33 | -1 | 0..33 | dirt, under everything except the pool |
| Sidewalk | 0..33 | 0 | 0 | smooth_stone, one row along the street |
| Driveway (concrete) | 1..8 | 0 | 1..21 | smooth_stone; joint rows of light_gray_concrete at z=4,8,12,16 |
| Front yard (desert) | 9..33 | 0 | 1..7 | sand; gravel beds at x=22..30 z=1..5 and x=10..16 z=1..5 |
| Stepping-pad path | 18..20 | 0 | 1, 3, 5 | three 3x1 smooth_stone pads in the sand (sand between them) |
| Entry landing | 18..20 | 0 | 6..7 | smooth_stone, under the eave |
| Side strips | 0 (x) / 32..33 | 0 | 1..25 | x=0: sand; x=32..33: sand |
| MAIN HOUSE (shell) | 10..31 | 1..5 | 8..25 | 22 wide x 18 deep; walls on the perimeter |
| Main roof (incl. overhangs) | 9..32 | 6..7 | 6..27 | low gable, ridge along x; see ROOFS |
| Beam ends (exposed tails) | each beam line | 5 | 5 and 28 | 1 cell past the roof edge, front and back |
| ATRIUM (open courtyard, open to the sky) | 17..21 | 1..open | 12..17 | 5x6; glass ring on x=16, x=22, z=11, z=18 |
| Entry recess | 18..20 | 2..4 | 8 | air niche; the door wall sits back at z=9 |
| Stone feature wall | 11..17 | 1..4 | 7 | freestanding 1-thick leaf, 1 proud of the north wall (z=8) |
| CARPORT | 0..9 | 1..5 | 7..21 | flat roof deck y=5 on posts; open N, W; screen at S |
| Carport posts | x=1 | 1..4 | z=8, 14, 20 | dark_oak_log, 1x1 |
| Carport beams | 0..9 | 4 | z=8, 14, 20 | dark_oak_log axis x; the deck sits on them |
| Carport breeze-block screen | 1..9 | 1..4 | 21 | pierced: checkerboard of white_concrete and AIR (holes left open) |
| CAR (reserved, see RESERVED) | 3..5 | 1..2 | 1..7 | parked nose to the street on the driveway, in front of the carport |
| Chimney (fireplace part) | 20..21 | 2..8 | 21..22 | rises through the roof 1 above the ridge band |
| Back patio | 10..31 | 0 | 26..28 | smooth_stone, under/behind the south eave |
| Pool deck | 11..24 | 0 | 29..33 | smooth_stone around the pool |
| KIDNEY POOL (reserved) | 13..22 | -2..0 | 29..32 | see RESERVED for the exact cells |
| Back lawn | 0..10 & 25..33 | 0 | 26..33 | grass_block (x=0..9 z=22..33 included) |
| Palms | (12,3), (30,4), (29,31) | 1..7 | — | jungle trunk + crown, reserved |
| Cactus cluster | 23..29 | 1..3 | 2..4 | on the gravel bed, reserved |
| Mailbox | 9 | 1..2 | 1 | low post + box at the head of the driveway |

## ROOFS

**Main roof: built BY HAND (no preset).** No `$MCD roof` preset fits a mid-century roof: every preset has a pitch of 0.5 or more, and the brief wants a very low gable. The low pitch is the identity, so the roof is a stepped slab gable with the ridge running E-W (along x), its slopes facing the street and the garden. It covers x=9..32 (1 cell of overhang at each gable end) and z=6..27 (2 cells of overhang front and back):

| band | z rows | block / half | y |
|---|---|---|---|
| A, eaves | 6..10 and 23..27 | bottom slab | 6 |
| B | 11..13 and 20..22 | top slab | 6 |
| C | 14..15 and 18..19 | bottom slab | 7 |
| Ridge | 16..17 | top slab | 7 |

- Rise: 1.5 blocks over a 10-cell half-span, the near-flat Eichler gable. The highest point is y=7.
- **Fascia:** the outermost ring (z=6, z=27, x=9, x=32) uses dark_oak_slab at the same half as its band, so a dark line runs round the eave.
- **Atrium hole:** no roof over x=17..21, z=12..17. The edge of the hole is dark_oak_slab, as fascia.
- **Chimney hole:** no roof at x=20..21, z=21..22.
- **Under band C:** the y=6 cells over the interior are air (a raised ceiling vault). The two gable ends close them with glass (see OPENINGS), and so does the atrium ring where it crosses band C (x=16 and x=22, y=6, z=14..17, glass).
- **Beams (exposed):** dark_oak_log with axis z, at y=5 on each beam line x=10,13,...,31, running z=5..28. They pass through the north and south header courses. Inside the house they are ceiling beams with 3 cells of headroom (y=2..4) below them; between the beams the ceiling is at y=5. Outside, they carry the overhang and stick out 1 cell past the fascia at z=5 and z=28. Where the beam on x=19 crosses the atrium it stays as an open beam over the courtyard.
- **Carport roof:** a flat deck, hand built: smooth_stone_slab (bottom half) at y=5 over x=0..9, z=7..21, with a dark_oak_slab fascia on its outer edges (x=0, z=7, z=21). It sits one level below the main roof's west eave (x=9, y=6). The two horizontal planes layered against each other are the mid-century signature.

## FACADES

All walls are white stucco (white_concrete). Every outer wall has the same three layers:

| layer | y | block |
|---|---|---|
| Base (slab edge) | 1 | smooth_stone |
| Body | 2..4 | white stucco, glass or posts |
| Header course | 5 | dark_oak_planks, a continuous dark band under the eave |

The beam ends cross the header.

**North (street, z=8): mostly blank.** From west to east:
- **x=10..17:** blank stucco. In front of it, the **ledgestone feature wall** stands at z=7, x=11..17, y=1..4. It is 1 proud and freestanding, mud_bricks mixed with ~25% packed_mud for the stacked-stone texture.
